bullets: Built a layer-7 HTTP load balancer and reverse proxy in Go (standard library plus yaml.v3), selecting backends in a custom RoundTripper beneath httputil.ReverseProxy so header handling, streaming and upgrades stayed in the standard library

Implemented round-robin, nginx-style smooth weighted round-robin and weighted least-connections; least-connections delivered 2.7x round-robin's throughput (7,182 vs 2,621 req/s) and cut p90 latency from 51.7 ms to 8.5 ms with one 50 ms backend in the pool. Also fixed a weighted round-robin bug where leftover weight debt sent request bursts to one backend after the pool changed

Designed layered failure handling (active health checks with rise/fall thresholds, passive checks on live traffic, and retries of idempotent requests on a different backend), cutting failed requests when a backend was killed under load from 4,327 to 0 and detection time from 2,979 ms to 18 ms

Instrumented the proxy with lock-free, atomics-based Prometheus metrics (latency histogram, per-backend responses and errors, up and in-flight gauges, state transitions) and a JSON admin status API on a separate port
Wrote 44 test cases at 92.7% statement coverage, run with the Go race detector in GitHub Actions alongside a Docker Compose smoke test that stops a backend and asserts zero client errors

Packaged as a multi-stage distroless Docker image with a Compose demo, a closed-loop load generator and a reproducible benchmark suite, measuring 8,562 req/s through the proxy vs 23,177 req/s direct on a shared 12-thread laptop, delivered through 8 issue-linked PRs
summary: Layer-7 load balancer in Go with three balancing strategies, active and passive health checks, retries and Prometheus metrics, benchmarked under load and failure.
title: HTTP Load Balancer & Reverse Proxy in Go
